newsitem.title: UGANDA: Ugandan rebels on the run, minister says.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan rebels on the run, minister says.

text.p: Rebels who have attacked towns in western Uganda are hiding in remote mountain areas from pursuing Ugandan troops, Minister of State for Defence Amama Mbabazi told reporters on Sunday.

He denied local press reports that Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) rebels attacked Kasese, western Uganda, on Saturday, but said defence officials were investigating a "shoot-out" at Kasese police station during the night.
ADF rebels had earlier circulated warnings to Kasese residents that they would attack on Saturday -- causing a panic-stricken exodus from the railhead town.

Mbabazi said the security situation was still serious, with small groups of rebels raiding isolated villages for food and medical supplies. But local defence units were being organised to protect villages.
He said the rebels, who numbered about 1,300 when they invaded from the neighbouring Democratic Republic of the Congo last month, were now down to about 400.
They were hiding in remote areas of the Ruwenzori mountain range -- the Mountains of the Moon -- pursued by the Uganda army.
Several thousand villagers have fled the remote area near the Congo border since the attacks. Some have taken refuge in the new Congo, while others are in Ugandan centres away from the border.
